Sponsor: Lexar Thor DDR5 RAM on Amazon https://geni.us/AuxUm9
We bought a PowerColor RX 7900 XT Hellhound for $720 recently and we're revisiting it for a 2023 refresh. It *WAS* the cheapest card for a little bit, and hopefully it will be again. The 7900 XT has changed price a lot over the last year, meaning the value proposition could have changed alongside that. Most recently, we've seen swings from $850 to $720, then $800, and now there are some back at $750 again -- but all of these are transient, of course, and the conclusion ends up being a more nuanced "if it costs THIS, then here's what we think." We'd assume some of the pricing chaos is due to GPU oversupply and some is due to impending holiday sales. Either way, we're revisiting the RX 7900 XT vs. the RTX 4070 Ti, RX 6950 XT, RTX 4070, and RX 7900 XTX (among other cards). Comment below with what older card you want us to revisit next!

While we are on the topic of Revisits, since you mentioned at the end of the program: As I had brought up a matter of weeks ago on Twitter, Vega 020 celebrates its Fifth Anniversary this upcoming November 0I8, the GPU that makes up the Radeon Instinct MI50/MI60 and Radeon VII has been around long enough now that the latter's Driver Maturity has put it in a position where many titles will witness it consistently run at about 05 to 07% faster than a 1080 Ti under multiple conditions and its OpenCL performance still makes it a powerhouse in Production applications that rely heavily on this type of workload, most notably Vegas Pro when handling AVC and HEVC renders with heavy use of Special Effects (do take note though that using Twixtor and especially Vegas' AI suite will make it chug; the latter can make it hit Temperature Junction MAX regardless of the footage, resolution, and framerate).

comments.text:
In regard to raytracing in Cyberpunk, i just made about 100 comparative screenshots, turning Raytracing on and off and the result is quite baffling. Yes, raytracing rules in specular reflections, but that is about it. Most of the screenshots show rather a sort of sidegrade , not an upgrade. Specular reflections are kind of rare and on diffuse reflections, raytracing doesnt have an advantage and sometimes even looks less good.

What baffled me most though, is that the whole raytracing is better in cyberpunk, is a bit of a scam. I have noticed light sources, that have not been there without RTX, as well as plain white light sources, which have been changed into fancy colors, with RTX enabled. So the better looks are not an rtx achievement at all, in some cases. Plus i suppose, one got to keep in mind, that the raytracing in Cyberpunk is not a parallel development, but has been added to cyberpunk, while looking at the non rtx mode and purposely finetuning it to look better, and improve on the looks. Hardly a fair fight. Their favorite technique seems to have been, to make certain surfaces look darker with rtx on. However, some screenshots also show normal rasterization having darker surfaces, so it is again most likely a matter of finetuning the lightsources, as well for rtx as also for rasterization.

To me it appears, that raytracing is pretty much a FOMO strategy that nvidia uses, to create the illusion of an advantage, that wont be there for at least another couple years. Plus we gotta keep in mind, all that power that raytracing swallows, is missing when we play high end VR, which makes the whole direction of raytracing kind of doubtful. Especially considering that on most occasions, it is a sidegrade and not an upgrade, except for specular reflections.

Can't you at gamer nexus, dissect raytracing in cyberpunk and pop that bubble a bit? It is not a healthy direction to push raytracing that much, considering performance cost vs visual quality gain. To me it seems, all it is, is a fomo strategy and not even a very good one, at this point of development. Have your whole team play the game and take random screenshots of normal locations, that do not have specular reflections and then analyze them. To me, the second highest raytracing setting, looked fine, but not really better than max settings without rtx, in 95 percent of the cases.
comments.author: @suntoxx9667

Kind of detached from the floor. In non raytracing mode, they added the shadows you would expect, but they exagerated them, so they look kind of wrong. comments.text:
Techpowerup has the 7900XT at 85% the performance of the 7900XTX. That means that if the XTX is $1000 and the XT is $850 you're getting shafted for 4GB of VRAM. Plain and simple. 

At $800 the overall value is sorta the same but you're at least getting a little bit better perf/$ value. 

At $750 we're starting to see something that approaches a value proposition. 85% the performance for 75% the price is juuust about where you start to ignore the 4GB VRAM and go "20GB is probably going to last me until performance become the main issue anyway....". 

But that's if you're evaluating the card in a vacuum.

At $700 it's "The 4070ti is 10% slower in raster, only has 12GB VRAM and is $100 bucks more... that's a straight deal". 

But that is AMD's dilemma: Nvidia just have to lower the price of the 4070ti to $770 (13 available on Newegg at that price) and it's back to "Naaah.. I'll pay the 10% extra for Nvidia's features and convince myself that 12GB isn't going to become a problem anytime soon". Nvidia makes so much better margins than AMD that they can afford playing this game until AMD can't go lower without the investors suggesting that RTG should just be laid off entirely.... So why would they bother? The thing is: They won't. They're pricing exactly good enough to keep the customers who're either allergic to green or just principally buy the best raster performance per dollar card in their price bracket.

TL;DR: People only want AMD to compete so they can get cheaper Nvidia cards.

comments.text:
Seeing Geizhals prices is very much appreciated - I exclusively search for tech to buy there because they actually have ROCK SOLID product data sheets that you can filter super easily for. It's almost like they want people to be able to use search and filters, it's amazing. It also showing me which retailers have the cheapest prices is the cherry on top, I've found a few smaller tech retailers that have great customer service and often even better prices than Amazon through Geizhals and I'd have never found them otherwise.

As some others have pointed out, Geizhals data is not 100% indicative of the whole of Europe, but I don't think you'll find any other data aggregator with anywhere close to this reliable and in-depth data and it should reflect the general ballpark of pricing in most of the EU.

Edit: Geizhals actually helped me make the decision of getting a 7900XT back when it was deemed to be "badly positioned/priced" but all the other recommendations were just... more expensive in the EU - the 7900XT was the only one even close to MSRP, everything else was wildly above to the point where even the XTX was so distant the XT didn't feel like an upsell anymore at all (XT at ~900€ vs XTX at the very least at 1200€). Having a fairly broad overview over the market with their listings really helped me reevaluate all the reviews I've seen (rightly) calling the XT too expensive in the context of the rest of the market here - most of the time the relative pricing is close enough to American prices so these reviews still work, but this launch was just a mess.

You do not review what I play:  Elder Scrolls, not for 3 years--World of WarCraft, and for the last 3 years--Guild Wars 2.  I went from a X-99 PC to an Aorus Master X570 when my X-99 MB died, with first a 3600X then 5800X, ram from my X-99 (4x4 2800 Corsair Dominator) to 4x8 3600cl16 from GSKILL with an EVGA 1080Ti FTW3.  My monitor was a ROG 27' IPS 165Hz PG279 and currently a Hisense 4K TV 55U8G (the ROG is back in its box).  No bench marking tools but:  I noticed a difference going to the 3600X then the 5800X and again when my budget allowed better ram.  The 1080Ti did not allow max pretty, but handled 4K just fine for the 3 titles I play(ed).  No RT, but "pretty" is well down the list of my requirements.  It IS a nice to have, but smooth game play and fun to play (for me) well outweighs pretty.  From my limited games playing experience, I'm always surprised at how low the 1080Ti is on your charts when I play at 4K (maybe my EVGA was a "golden sample"?).  My grandkids get my hand-me-downs, so they are always happy when I upgrade.  I did finally buy last Prime Day a Hellhound 7900XTX and "pretty" is maxed out, which makes buying a 4090 rather pointless.  My guess is the 7800XT would have been an amazing upgrade as well at $500-530.

There are "World Bosses" in each of the starting areas (GW2 event timer for when and where) you could take a L8+ avatar and see what performance CPU/GPU combinations have.  The basic game is free to play, no save points per se, so just getting to a "World Boss" and participating will increase your avatars level, which wouldn't affect how well or poorly a CPU/GPU does.  Take avatars to where each of the Bosses are, so you could test different combinations a bit quicker rather than waiting for the one Boss to respawn.  Yes, the number of people at any particular Boss could affect the numbers you get, but "many" versus "lots more" would still be a valid result for how the combination handles a workload.

comments.text:
You already know it... AMD wins practically every time at the entry level because RT is useless at this performance tier and DLSS Quality is uglier at 1080p than turning down settings (I hate calling $400 entry level, but it is what it is).

At $400 the 6800 is the bees knees while it lasts. Precisely as fast as the 7700XT,  has 16GB, only uses 5W more but is $50 cheaper. Against the $400 3070 it's 10% faster and 8GB at this price is a joke nobody's laughing at.

At $320 the 6700XT is 5% faster than the $330 3060ti but 12GB vs 8GB.

At $240 for the 6650XT and $260 for the 3060 12GB it's a little less straight forward as the 6650XT is 17% faster but the 3060 has 12GB. Had the 6650XT been $220 I would have handed AMD this one, but as it stands it's simply a matter of preference between performance or longevity. I personally lean towards cranking texture quality up, and other settings down, so I think the $20 for 4GB more is worth it. But $40 for 4GB and a performance hit would be a sour deal at this price point.

At $200 for the 6600 Nvidia simply doesn't have an answer. It's 26% faster than the $180 3050 at a performance tier where 26% is a big effing deal. The 3050 is worth precisely $150 and not a single cent more.

Now, some will argue that the 6800/3070 are 1440p GPUs so DLSS is an argument, but I'll point to recent game releases where even 1440p Low with DLSS Quality is a mouthful for the 3070, and thus state that anyone buying last gen right now need to step a resolution notch down compared to how they were originally marketed, unless they want to be sorry in short order.

(All performance numbers are from the Techpowerup's GPU database which generally lines up for raster with Hardware Unboxed's 50+ game benchmark averages)

comments.text:
I am here, yet again, to make sure everyone (who actually reads this comment) knows that some 6900xt cards are better than the 6950xt
Normal 6900xt uses the navi21 xtx die
6950xt uses a different variant called the navi21 kxtx, which is faster than navi21 xtx
But SOME 6900xts use a variant called navi21 xtxh.
The xtxh die used in SOME 6900xts is faster than the kxtx die used in the 6950xt (when overclocking)
This is why if you compare the 6900xt to the 6950xt in the HWBot benchmark rankings, the 6900xt leads the 6950xt in every single benchmark.

This makes no difference whatsoever outside of overclocking, but i feel it is worth noting because xtxh die 6900xts can often be found for less money than the cheapest 6950xts. I recently saw the asrock 6900xt OC formula (which is one of a handful of cards that are guaranteed to be an xtxh die) for $550 new on Amazon.
Some of the xtxh die 6900xts are the asrock OC formula, powercolor red devil ultimate, sapphire toxic (air cooled model), msi gaming Z trio, xfx merc 319 limited, asus strix LC TOP (watercooled w/aio), powercolor liquid devil ultimate (w/waterblock), gigabyte xtreme waterforce (w/waterblock), sapphire toxic extreme (watercooled w/aio), and xfx speedster zero (w/waterblock)


Happy hunting everyone!

I went from a 6700XT/1440p to an XTX/1440p. I was already getting 85-95FPS in all my games with the 6700XT with mixed settings and it looked good. Back in the day throwing 30% more polygons at an object made it look significantly better. These days doubling the polygon count only just makes a difference.

comments.text:
@thelaughingmanofficial  About 5 years ago I worked at a retail store that got in trouble over this. Unless something has changed, the laws vary state to state, there isn't a federal law that protects people, my retailer just went with CA laws since they were the strictest and had a large enough market to make them care. 

The law basically boiled down to the product had to be sold at retail price for 30 days before it could be discounted. Nothing about selling it at retail for 30 days, discounting it, jacking up the price for 30 days, then discounting it again. Maybe the laws have changed since I worked there, but judging from all the retailers I see doing this, I doubt it. More likely that people just don't understand the law, and freak out when companies legally manipulate prices in an anti-consumer way.
comments.author: @CptSweetCheeksJr

comments.text:
​ @AeriFyrein  laws are always vague like that. It is meant to make it harder for companies to abuse by going around the law. Like if they would say 2 weeks, companies could increase the price exactly 14 days before and the judge could do nothing. Saying "meaningful amount of time" give the judge more flexibility.

But way too often, when the company (especially with big companies, such as Amazon and Newegg or in other domains Microsoft, Google, Apple, etc) is considered to use illegal practice, the fine is smaller than the benefit of using that tactic, so they don't really care.
